name: Richard Garriott
category: Video game designer / RPG founder (Ultima, Origin Systems)
milestone_by_age_26: Commercially published Akalabeth (1980) at about age 18–19 and Ultima I (1981) at ~20, then co-founded Origin Systems in 1983 at age 21–22 to publish Ultima III.
early_history_summary: Born in Cambridge, England (July 4, 1961) to NASA scientist-astronaut Owen Garriott and artist Helen Garriott; raised in the U.S. with early computer access. Built dungeon-crawl games in high school (Akalabeth), sold via ComputerLand and California Pacific, then founded Origin Systems with brother Robert and others.
family_context_summary: Son of NASA astronaut Owen Garriott and artist mother Helen; middle/upper-professional household with unusual science access.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a NASA scientist-astronaut (Skylab 3, STS-9); mother contributed art for early game packaging—adjacent creative/science support rather than game-industry dynasty.
primary_early_advantage_tags: NASA father, early computer access, sibling cofounder, Apple II era, high-school shipping
evidence_summary: Garriott shipped commercial CRPGs as a teenager (Akalabeth/Ultima) and co-founded Origin Systems by 22, defining computer RPGs. Family NASA/science context and rare early computer access amplified prior reps; brother Robert was a durable cofounder. Later Origin/EA career and private spaceflight built on that teenage breakout.
starting_point: Born Cambridge, England 1961 to NASA astronaut father Owen Garriott and artist mother; raised with early computer access in the U.S.
current_position: Game designer and private astronaut (Lord British); continues entrepreneurial game projects after Origin, NCSoft, and spaceflight career.

trajectory.event: Commercially published Akalabeth via California Pacific; sold tens of thousands of copies.
Released Ultima I, launching one of the defining computer RPG franchises.
Co-founded Origin Systems with brother Robert and partners to publish Ultima III and later titles.
Origin acquired by Electronic Arts as Ultima remained a flagship RPG series.
Ultima Online launched, pioneering the commercial MMORPG category.
Flew to the International Space Station as a private astronaut.

name: Toby Fox
milestone_by_age_26: Released Undertale on September 15, 2015 at age 23, a solo-developed RPG that became a global indie breakout with critical acclaim and massive cultural impact.
early_history_summary: Born Robert F. Fox on October 11, 1991 in Manchester, New Hampshire. Built early RPG Maker games and ROM hacks (including EarthBound Halloween Hack), composed for Homestuck as a teen/early 20s, then developed Undertale largely alone as writer, designer, and composer.
family_context_summary: Born in New Hampshire; detailed family financial/professional background not well documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: RPG Maker, EarthBound hacks, Homestuck music, solo indie, internet fandom
evidence_summary: Fox accumulated design and composition reps via fan communities and Homestuck before shipping Undertale solo at 23—an unusually complete multi-discipline breakout. Advantage stack is self-created online practice and taste rather than elite pedigree or capital.
starting_point: Born Manchester, New Hampshire, October 11, 1991; early creative path through RPG Maker, ROM hacks, and online composition communities.
current_position: Indie game developer and composer; continuing Deltarune episodic releases after Undertale's cultural breakout.

trajectory.event: Released EarthBound Halloween Hack and other early fan/ROM-hack work under FwugRadiation.
Began contributing music to the Homestuck webcomic community, building composition reputation.
Released Undertale, which became a landmark indie RPG and cultural phenomenon.
Began releasing Deltarune chapters set in a parallel universe to Undertale.
Continued Deltarune development and major platform soundtrack contributions.

name: Edmund McMillen
category: Indie game designer (Gish, Super Meat Boy, Binding of Isaac)
milestone_by_age_26: Released Gish (2004) at about age 24, which won Indie Game of the Year / Adventure Game of the Year honors and established him as a leading independent designer before Super Meat Boy and The Binding of Isaac.
early_history_summary: Born March 2, 1980 in Santa Cruz County, California; raised in a born-again Christian family with creative support from his grandmother. Produced Flash games and comics early, then shipped Gish with Cryptic Sea/Chronic Logic before later Team Meat and Binding of Isaac successes.
family_context_summary: Raised in Watsonville/Santa Cruz area in a born-again Christian family of Mexican descent; grandmother strongly supported his drawing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family religious context shaped later themes (Binding of Isaac); not a game-industry family dynasty.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Flash games, comics, grandmother support, indie awards, personal themes
evidence_summary: McMillen built a large body of Flash/indie work culminating in award-winning Gish at 24, then Super Meat Boy (2010) and Binding of Isaac (2011). Path is self-created creative repetition with online distribution, not elite institutions or inherited capital.
starting_point: Born March 2, 1980, Santa Cruz County, California; creative childhood drawing monsters with grandmother's support in a religious household.
current_position: Indie game designer/artist continuing solo and collaborative projects after Super Meat Boy, Binding of Isaac franchise, and later titles.

trajectory.event: Released Gish, winning major indie awards and establishing his design voice.
Released Flash Meat Boy and other experimental titles building toward console breakout.
Released Super Meat Boy with Tommy Refenes; featured in Indie Game: The Movie.
Released The Binding of Isaac, founding a long-running roguelike franchise.
Released The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth remake expanding the series.

name: Phil Fish
milestone_by_age_26: Quit studio work and opened Polytron Corporation as a startup in early 2008 (~age 23) after Fez was nominated for IGF awards; Fez had been announced in 2007 and won IGF Excellence in Visual Art in 2008.
early_history_summary: Born Philippe Poisson November 1, 1984 in Montreal; parents shared art/gaming interests (father translated Zelda into French). Graduated NAD game design (2004), worked at Ubisoft and Artificial Mind and Movement, co-founded Kokoromi experimental collective, then went indie with Fez/Polytron.
family_context_summary: Raised in Quebec; parents shared interests in art and gaming; father translated Zelda so they could play together.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents fostered gaming/art interest; not an industry dynasty.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Montreal game scene, NAD program, Kokoromi, IGF, indie wave
evidence_summary: Fish specialized early in game design, left AAA work to found Polytron by 23 with Fez already an IGF standout. Commercial Fez release came at 27 (2012), but company founding and festival recognition are clear ≤26 material milestones.
starting_point: Born Montreal 1984; raised in Quebec with parents who shared art and Nintendo gaming interests.
current_position: Former indie developer best known for Fez; largely stepped back from game development after Polytron/Fez controversies; occasional design contributions later.

trajectory.event: Graduated NAD Centre game design program in Montreal.
Announced Fez and co-ran experimental Kokoromi/GAMMA events.
Founded Polytron; Fez won IGF Excellence in Visual Art after he went fully indie.
Released Fez to critical acclaim; sold hundreds of thousands of copies.
Cancelled Fez 2 and publicly left game development after industry conflicts.
